author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Microsoft: Anti-Amazon Winner - Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)
text:
After a decade of failure in the smartphone and hardware sector, Microsoft ( MSFT ) is suddenly in a good position without exposure to that market. The company is even positioned as the savior to the Amazon ( AMZN ) empire driving the relative strength in the stock.
Image Source: Microsoft website
It's All Relative Over the last six months, Microsoft has seen the best relative performance of the giant tech stock group. In fact, the company has seen the only positive return in the period with Apple ( AAPL ), Facebook ( FB ), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG ) ( GOOGL ) and Amazon all taking big hits due to market issues such as smartphone weakness and data privacy concerns.
MSFT data by YCharts
The amazing part is that Microsoft has become the Switzerland in the tech giant space. The company that regularly ran afoul of regulators in the 2000s now is positively absent from the data privacy issues hitting all of these other tech giants outside of Apple.
The other good news is that Apple isn't in the enterprise cloud segment leaving Microsoft to duel with Amazon that has increasing concerns from consumers on data privacy. Not to mention competitors are afraid that the company is collecting information about their businesses to compete directly with them.
With Google, the company has plenty of data privacy concerns due to data collected from consumers on search and YouTube viewing habits. In addition, regulators in the EU have them in their sites similar to Microsoft in the last decade.
All of this leaves Microsoft as the clean cloud provider where consumers and enterprises aren't as worried about the data on the platform.
Anti-Amazon The Walgreens Boots Alliance ( WBA ) deal screams of the benefits of being the anti-Amazon enterprise cloud provider. Sure, the deal goes beyond just basic cloud services for the Walgreens employee base to interact with customer health solutions, but one major fact of the deal is that AWS wasn't a solution option. Winning deals with the best solution is ideal; winning deals as the anti-Amazon solution is just as good.
The deal is even more significant than just being a cloud win as Microsoft is taking over the majority of the IT infrastructure for WBA. Besides transitioning IT platforms to Microsoft Azure, the 380,000-employee base of WBA will shift to Microsoft 365.
According to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on the WBA deal:
Together with Walgreens Boots Alliance, we aim to deliver on this promise by putting people at the center of their health and wellness, combining the power of the Azure cloud and AI technology and Microsoft 365 with Walgreens Boots Alliance’s deep expertise and commitment to helping communities around the world lead healthier and happier lives.
The move follows Kroger ( KR ) moving to a split partnership with Azure and Google Cloud. The company formed a partnership with Microsoft to develop a Retail-as-a-Service (RaaS) offering to market to other retailers using Azure as the infrastructure for the service.
According to Ed Anderson ( via ZDNet ), research VP and analyst for Gartner, these moves in the retail space are primarily related to not wanting to work with Amazon:
Most retailers view AWS as a competitor and don't like feeding Amazon's business, even if it's through AWS. That certainly pushes retailers to consider other technology alternatives, including Microsoft and Google, when pursuing cloud, or cloud-based initiatives.
The good news for Microsoft is that Amazon has moved into healthcare recently, providing more opportunities to snag deals like the one with WBA.
Amazon has a huge lead in the enterprise cloud space via AWS. The Microsoft cloud revenue levels are misleading with the Office 365 numbers counted in their numbers. Based on this survey from Right Scale, Azure is closing the gap with AWS as more and more companies prefer to move towards a Microsoft solution over one from Amazon that competes with so many companies from retail to healthcare to media.
According to the numbers, AWS has about $20 billion in annual revenues. The market is growing rapidly so taking market share from AWS would provide a big catalyst for the growth at Microsoft even with a revenue base of $124 billion.
Not Cheap The biggest problem is that the stock isn't cheap. Microsoft became reasonable for those that acted in the December swoon, but the stock is already back to $108. My previous research had problems when Microsoft was trading in this range back last July.
MSFT data by YCharts
A prime reason to place Microsoft on a buy list for the next market selloff. Analysts forecast the company to earn $5.03 in FY20, so one should look at any dips below $100 over the summer as a prime entry point.
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that Microsoft is suddenly in a great place as the anti-Amazon in the cloud space without any data privacy issues swirling around the company. The stock valuation is a little stretched here, but Microsoft quickly turns appealing on any dips to $100 as the year passes and the market starts looking towards FY20 numbers. A 20x forward P/E ratio would be very tasty by the summer.
